pick.headline: Gorbachev awarded the Nobel Peace Prize
pick.summary: On October 15, 1990, the Nobel Committee awarded the Peace Prize to Mikhail Gorbachev.
pick.significance: The prize honoured his part in ending the Cold War, but was greeted coolly at home, where the economy was failing.
pick.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of October 16, 1990, carried Sofia BTA in English: President Zhelev congratulated Gorbachev on the Nobel Peace Prize as reward for helping dismantle the totalitarian system.

alternates.headline: Young officers overthrow General Romero in El Salvador
alternates.summary: On October 15, 1979, reformist military officers overthrew President Carlos Humberto Romero of El Salvador and formed a civilian-military junta.
alternates.significance: Washington backed the junta as an alternative to revolution after Somoza's fall in Nicaragua, but its reforms failed and El Salvador slid into civil war.
alternates.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of October 16, 1979, opened its El Salvador section with "Military Revolt Topples Government, Romero Flees," followed by items on his departure for Guatemala, the junta's members and an armed forces proclamation.
